decision.risk_area: security-sensitive code (csrf); public API contract (accepts helper)
decision.why: Three independent small fixes in separate middleware/helpers; 140 test files give a safety net. Sized per part, since the parts share no code. The top-level tier is the highest part tier.
decision.shared:
Run the relevant tests with: npx vitest --run <test file paths>
Do not commit.

parts.title: csrf skips OPTIONS
parts.text:
The csrf middleware rejects OPTIONS requests (for example CORS preflight)
when the Origin doesn't match. RFC 9110 defines OPTIONS as a safe method,
like GET and HEAD, so it should not be subject to CSRF validation.
parts.why: One-sentence change (treat OPTIONS like GET/HEAD in the origin check), verifiable by the existing csrf tests. Small local fix in a risk area, sized like any other change.

parts.title: etag If-None-Match whitespace
parts.text:
The etag middleware returns 200 with the full body instead of 304 when the
If-None-Match header has whitespace before a comma, e.g. `"a" , "b"`, even
though the current ETag is in the list. RFC 9110 allows optional whitespace
on both sides of the list delimiter.
parts.why: Pattern is stated in one sentence (trim each list entry before comparing), and the etag tests can verify it. No risk area involved.

parts.title: accepts() subtype wildcards
parts.text:
The `accepts()` helper's default matcher ignores subtype wildcards sent by
clients. With supports ['application/json', 'text/html'], `Accept: application/*`
falls back to the default instead of returning application/json. A subtype
wildcard (`type/*`) should match a supported type of that type. At the same
quality value an exact match takes precedence over a wildcard match. The global
wildcards `*/*` and `*` keep their current behavior: they fall through to the
configured default rather than picking a supported value.
parts.why: Needs precedence logic across quality values and must keep the global-wildcard behavior intact. Judgment inside one function, with tests to check against.

checks.reason: All three fixes are in place, and I found no regressions. The csrf middleware now treats OPTIONS as a safe method. The etag middleware splits If-None-Match on `\s*,\s*`, so whitespace before the comma is allowed. In accepts.ts, defaultMatch now resolves `type/*` to a supported value of that type, and at the same q an exact match sorts ahead of a wildcard. `*/*` and `*` still fall through to the default.
